contract: ../forecast-pages-consistency.md acceptance contract; design.MD shared typography and Forecast search/evidence rules.

accessibility.evidence: Production Playwright checks exercised labeled controls, keyboard location selection/dismissal, focus after clearing search, tab draft retention, native disclosures and 44px mobile targets. This is bounded browser coverage, not a full accessibility certification.

responsive.evidence: 18 routes were checked at 1366x768 and 390x844 in English and Arabic RTL (72 samples), including computed type roles and document overflow. Dataset/evaluation suites add 375, 768, 1024, 1440 and 1920 widths. Wide evidence tables keep local horizontal scrolling.

loading.evidence: forecast-search-usability.spec.ts exercises delayed lookup feedback and cancellation of superseded location requests.

empty.evidence: Dataset and evaluation histories distinguish an empty authorized dataset from no filter matches; reset and individual clear controls are exercised.

error.evidence: The location lookup failure/recovery test preserves the typed code and checks manual-code guidance and retry.

partial.evidence: Saved driver/base/demand reports retain missing dates, unknown ages, source-declared availability and excluded/conditional evidence rather than inferring values.

success.evidence: Populated saved-evidence suites verify exact values, disclosures, explicit filter application and embedded workbench paging/history navigation.

permission.evidence: Relevant suites retain tenant/location-scoped lookup, viewer mutation restrictions and hidden-record HTTP 404 assertions; local pgTAP also passed.

limitations: Chromium only; emulated CSS viewports, not physical-device certification.
No complete screen-reader or Safari/Firefox audit.
Existing untranslated copy uses the established English fallback; new labels have Arabic entries.
Full-page screenshot height can exceed the viewport.
Chromium native select line height reports normal; its font size, bounds and target height were checked separately.
No visual-similarity or test-coverage percentage is claimed.
